title: On the Algorithmic Bias of Aligning Large Language Models with RLHF

summary.claim: The KL regularization in standard RLHF distorts preferences and, in the extreme, causes preference collapse that nearly ignores minority preferences. PM RLHF fixes this by matching the response distribution to the preference distribution implied by the reward model.
summary.condition: Bradley-Terry-Luce/Plackett-Luce preference model assumed; OPT and Llama experiments, 29–41% better than standard RLHF.
summary.gap: (Inferred) The effect of preference matching on expressed confidence or calibration is not studied.
